page: UpCloud STARTER-2xCPU-16GB is a KVM-based virtual server belonging to the Starter family. It features 2 vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 9575F processor running at 2.0 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The CPU allocation is shared. The system is equipped with 16.0 GB of RAM, providing a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per core. Local storage consists of a bundled 50 GB SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark data reveals a stark contrast between single-core and multi-core performance. Single-core execution is highly competitive, with stress-ng single-core CPU performance, single-threaded gzip compression, and single-threaded bzip3 decompression all placing in the top 10% tier. However, multi-core and multi-threaded operations show limitations, likely due to the shared CPU allocation. The Passmark CPU score, Passmark database operations, and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression fall into the bottom 25% tier. Memory bandwidth remains moderate, with large-block read and write speeds averaging 68.93 GB/sec and 50.93 GB/sec respectively.

This server offers a cost-effective profile for memory-intensive workloads that do not demand sustained, parallelized CPU throughput. The high memory density relative to the low vCPU count makes it a strong candidate for lightweight caching layers, small-scale web serving, and memory-heavy utility scripts. However, it is poorly suited for parallel processing, heavy database operations, or medium-to-large language model inference, as indicated by the weak multi-threaded benchmarks and poor 7B LLM prompt processing speeds.
